amendments.title: Do not censor post-contact model failures with the pre-event liveness screen
amendments.problem: The original unconditional 8-second clean liveness screen was designed to reject routes where ORION stalls before reaching the hazard. Applying it after a contact-like event censors the most severe model outcomes, because collision-induced blocking is itself an outcome rather than an environment failure.

prospective_rule.pre_contact_or_no_contact: If the ego remains below 0.25 m/s for more than 8.0 continuous simulation seconds before any zero-gap OBB contact or other serious safety event, cancel and classify the replay as clean-liveness invalid.
prospective_rule.after_serious_geometry_or_evaluator_even: Do not cancel using the liveness fast screen. Allow the evaluator to terminate naturally or reach the Slurm wall-time. Record collision, blocking, timeout, route completion and traffic infractions as model outcomes.
prospective_rule.runtime_environment_invalidity: Sensor timeout, CARLA/RPC failure, missing map, process crash, Slurm OOM, or unavailable safety telemetry remain environment/runtime invalid and are not model outcomes.
prospective_rule.event_discovery_validity: A terminal eligible evaluator record is required for an official endpoint. Route completion of 100 percent and absence of blocking are not prerequisites when the purpose is discovering native model failures.
prospective_rule.paired_experiment_eligibility: A retained failure route still requires a separately frozen paired protocol; this amendment alone does not make it confirmation evidence.

amendments.retrospective_boundary: Job 1086149 remains a partial, nonterminal diagnostic under the original rule and is not relabeled as an official collision. It may motivate one explicitly labeled confirmation replay under this amended rule.

amendments.title: Treat low speed as an outcome diagnostic rather than an automatic cancellation rule in native difficulty discovery

triggering_observation.visual_context: Ego is queued behind vehicles at a red traffic signal; low speed is lawful and expected in this scene.

amendments.problem: A context-free low-speed threshold confounds environment failure with legal signal waiting, collision-induced blocking, and model-induced false stops. All three latter behaviors are relevant closed-loop outcomes for the present discovery objective.

superseding_rule.low_speed: Record longest continuous speed below 0.25 m/s, total stopped time, route progress and official blocked/timeout infractions, but do not automatically cancel a native difficulty-discovery route for low speed alone.
superseding_rule.runtime_environment_invalidity: Cancel or exclude only for sensor timeout, CARLA/RPC failure, missing map, process crash, Slurm OOM, unavailable safety telemetry, or another explicit infrastructure error.
superseding_rule.model_outcomes: Collision, traffic-rule violation, legal waiting, false stopping, vehicle_blocked, scenario timeout, route timeout and incomplete route progress remain evaluator/model outcomes.
superseding_rule.terminal_requirement: An eligible terminal evaluator record is required for an official endpoint; nonterminal partial traces remain diagnostic only.

amendments.retrospective_boundary: This rule does not relabel cancelled job 1086149. It applies to Route196 job 1086150, Route201 job 1086151 and the queued Route179 confirmation replay job 1086170.

amendments.title: Activate the preregistered reserve routes as additional clean native-event discovery cases

triggering_observation.platform_state: Route196 completed with a valid evaluator endpoint, Route201 continued to advance normally, and the validated gpu4 node remained stable enough to queue additional work.
triggering_observation.resource_boundary: Only gpu4 is currently validated for the required CARLA Vulkan runtime. Apparent idle accelerator capacity on other nodes is not treated as usable without a successful runtime validation.
triggering_observation.scientific_reason: Additional native-event geometries are useful for separating frontal, crossing, and junction-interaction failures and for avoiding control conclusions from a single retained collision case.

prospective_rule.submission_policy: The jobs may be queued together so Slurm can backfill genuine capacity, but their scientific order remains the preregistered reserve order. No learned, constant, shuffled, oracle, hazard/nohazard matrix, or adapter-controlled condition is activated by this amendment.
prospective_rule.evaluation: Use the same terminal evaluator and continuous TTC/gap diagnostics defined by the base protocol and the preceding low-speed amendment.

submission_record.invalid_reason: PILOT_ROUTE_DIR was omitted at submission, so each job failed in one second before CARLA startup while looking in the unrelated default pilot route directory.
submission_record.scientific_status: The fail-fast jobs are submission-configuration errors and produce no experimental result.

amendments.claim_boundary: These routes remain mechanism-development and native-event-discovery cases selected from published ORION reference failures. They are not held-out confirmation evidence and do not show that any failure was caused by observation uncertainty.

amendments.title: Add a control-trace progress watchdog after a mid-route CARLA tick stall

triggering_observation.failure_signature: The agent log and control trace stopped advancing after a real control frame, evaluator GPU utilization remained at zero, the Python evaluator waited, and the CARLA process continued without producing another tick for more than seven minutes.
triggering_observation.slurm_final_state: CANCELLED by user after confirmed no-progress interval

amendments.classification: CARLA/tick runtime environment failure; nonterminal diagnostic only

prospective_runtime_rule.on_trigger: Terminate the evaluator, let the outer runner clean up CARLA, write runtime_progress_watchdog.json, and exit nonzero with code 124.
prospective_runtime_rule.scientific_separation: The watchdog observes frame production only. It does not inspect ego speed, TTC, route progress, collisions, traffic lights, UQ, or control values, so lawful waiting, false stopping, and collision-induced blocking remain model/evaluator outcomes as long as control frames continue.

amendments.retry_policy: Job 1086151 is not a Route201 result and may receive one explicitly labeled runtime retry after the watchdog is deployed.

runtime_retry_submission.invalid_pending_reason: Cancelled before start because it inherited the same omitted PILOT_ROUTE_DIR submission error.
runtime_retry_submission.replacement_condition: clean_off with the correct native-collision-discovery route directory and the deployed progress watchdog

amendments.retrospective_boundary: The partial trace may be summarized for diagnostics but is ineligible for retention, endpoint comparison, or any safety claim.

amendments.title: Classify the Route179 confirmation as collision-positive but runtime-invalid and stop further retries

observed_result.runtime_failure: SPEED sensor missing for strict current frame 4666 after all other sensor tags arrived; 60-second sensor bundle timeout raised SensorReceivedNoData.

amendments.classification: Strong collision-reproduction diagnostic with evaluator/geometry actor agreement, but not a runtime-valid official endpoint because the evaluator marked the run ineligible after an infrastructure sensor failure.
amendments.retry_decision: Do not run a third Route179 replay. Route197 job 1086450 already supplies a runtime-valid 100-percent-complete, evaluator-aligned native collision for mechanism development, so another 192G/A800 Route179 retry has no necessary incremental role.
amendments.claim_boundary: Jobs 1086149 and 1086170 together show repeatable contact-like behavior on Route179, but neither may be counted in the official retained endpoint set. Their traces and GIFs remain diagnostic only.

amendments.title: Isolate concurrent CARLA instances with non-overlapping ten-port lanes

triggering_observation.failure_stage: CARLA startup before the first control frame
triggering_observation.concurrent_job: Route209 job 1086451 was already using RPC port 26451; CARLA also occupies adjacent streaming and secondary ports, so assigning 26452 and 26453 to the next jobs caused overlap.

amendments.classification: Runtime port-allocation error; both jobs produced no experimental result.

prospective_runtime_rule.scientific_separation: Port selection depends only on the Slurm job id and is independent of route, model outputs, safety telemetry, UQ and controls.

amendments.retry_policy: Route210 clean_off and the already-authorized Route201 runtime retry may each be resubmitted once with the isolated port scheme. No additional experimental condition is activated.

amendments.title: Retain Route210 as a second runtime-valid native crossing-collision development case

observed_result.weather: native night and rain; clean observation condition, not a corruption label

amendments.causal_direction_diagnostic: The retained actor approached from approximately 50.7 m ahead, developed a finite predicted OBB collision at about t=13.0 s, crossed laterally into the ego left-turn path, and contacted at t=15.05 s while ego speed remained about 4.70 m/s. Earlier bounded slowing is therefore directionally plausible rather than obviously adverse.

global_density_uq_diagnostic.interpretation: Operational global anomaly lead with measurable clean-scene activation burden; not evidence of spatial localization, task relevance, semantic UQ correctness, or uncertainty causation.

amendments.selection_and_execution_boundary: Retain Route210 as a secondary task-event oracle candidate and clean-night specificity diagnostic. Route197 remains the first frozen oracle case. This observed result does not authorize a Route210 oracle, learned governor, constant, shuffled, corruption, or matrix job without a new prospective amendment after the Route197 mechanism result.

amendments.title: Classify Route209 as an overconservative partial diagnostic followed by a watchdog-confirmed runtime failure
amendments.classification: The prolonged clean low-speed behavior is an overconservative/blocked diagnostic, not an official blocked endpoint. The subsequent CARLA tick stall makes the replay runtime-invalid and ineligible for a safety endpoint or route-completion comparison.
amendments.retry_decision: Do not retry Route209. Runtime-valid native vehicle collisions are already retained on Route197 and Route210, while Route209 contributes a useful specificity/overconservatism diagnostic but no necessary additional mechanism test worth another 192G/A800 replay.
amendments.claim_boundary: Route209 may be used to illustrate that low global Density UQ does not guarantee progress and that uncertainty-triggered slowing cannot fix every planning failure. It may not be counted as a completed no-collision route, an official blocked result, or evidence of improved safety.

amendments.title: Retain the Route201 runtime retry as a valid native actor-flow collision
amendments.classification: Runtime-valid, evaluator/geometry-aligned native vehicle collision retained for mechanism development and future route-level replication; not held-out confirmation.
amendments.clean_discovery_stop_rule: The frozen clean native-discovery batch is complete. Route197, Route210 and Route201 provide runtime-valid 100-percent-complete native vehicle collisions, so no further clean discovery routes are submitted before the separated adapter sidecar and task-event oracle are evaluated.
amendments.claim_boundary: The collision establishes a native interaction failure and severe TTC exposure. It does not establish observation uncertainty as the cause, adapter correctness, or uncertainty-aware safety improvement.
